note: tester.38 release manifest, started from the tester.37 manifest: the kmd and control rows move to the main commit with BD-292, BD-293, BD-295, BD-297 and the stage 2 queue reset of node 2; every other row keeps its tester.37 commit. BD-315: the system, wow64, desktop, zink and gl rows move to the t38/bd315-uqueue-* heads (global locks deleted at unload; the system head also has the util tests Windows build fix), and recipe_commit to the main commit with BD-317 (the RADV host tests link the real monitored fence). BD-211: the zink and gl rows move to merges of their BD-315 heads with the memstream temporary-file fix. rc1 (main 99a91dc8): the kmd, control, control-exe, router, d3d11 shell and state-worker rows move to main 99a91dc8, and the kmd rows to main b9f5e3bb with BD-321 (BD-205, BD-296, BD-306, BD-307, BD-298, BD-291, bd309), because main had commits under their source paths that they did not ship. BD-308/BD-309 (rc1): the dxvk engine rows (x64 and x86) move to dxvk t38/bd309-offer f9c4f228 (engine ABI 1.6, PrepareOffer) and the hosted ICD rows (x64 and x86) to mesa t38/bd309-hosted-t38 8b7160da (bc250GetMemoryAllocation), so that the d3d11 shell at 99a91dc8 gives offered engine resources to the kernel. rc2 (set-rc2, version 0.7.216.110-tester.38 kept, so the rc2 zips have the rc1 names; DriverVer equal to rc1, so an rc1 installation must be uninstalled before rc2 is installed; main 4e3867f9): the kmd, d3d11 shell, router, control, control-exe and state-worker rows move to main 4e3867f9 with BD-307 (WddmVersionCap, default WDDM 2.9; state catalog 02c7eed4) and BD-327 (engine worker memory scope of the d3d11 shell), and the dxvk engine rows and the d3d11 shell input dxvk to dxvk 87f730aa (engine ABI 1.7), because the BD-327 shell needs that engine. The d3d12 shell, engine12, hosted, adl and extra rows do not read driver/state and keep their rc1 commits. rc3 (0.7.216.111, ranks above rc1/rc2 and tester.37): the kmd, router, control, control-exe and state-worker rows and recipe_commit move to the main head with the BD-195 and BD-329 fixes, BD-324, the BD-223 caps DDIs and planes clamp, and BD-319; the d3d11 and d3d12 shell rows move to the head with the BD-200 shell part; the system, hosted, wow64 and desktop rows move to the BD-200 Fix A heads. The containment list names the fix commits that the containment gate checks in their rows.

outputs.pair_skew: The x86 row 90ab0352 and the x64 row a55f1b50 are the lines 96bae368 and cd3b0dda with the same two BD-200 commits each: the WDDM2 winsys holds the replaced preamble objects until the work of the queue retires (x86 676c8049, x64 2880180d), and it counts the AssumeNotInUse destroys that the host took (x86 90ab0352, x64 a55f1b50). The pair before that: The x86 row 96bae368 and the x64 row cd3b0dda are the lines b11faa28 and 9e14530f with the BD-315 change: u_queue and the WDDM2 Vulkan runtime delete their global locks when the ICD unloads (x86 a26c16ff and 96bae368, x64 c6c3c0c1 and d43c47d5). The x64 row also has the Windows build fix of the util tests (cd3b0dda), which changes only test files. The pair before that: The x86 row b11faa28 and the x64 row 9e14530f are the lines a45cf31d and 3b660ba0 with two merges each: BD-290, the tail of a compute buffer copy whose last thread would load past the source range copied with CP DMA (1f56cdaa, ba1df9df), and BD-200(a), a VK_SYNC_WAIT_PENDING wait that returns at submission and not at completion (df436d78, c7456a94). The pair before that: The x86 row a45cf31d and the x64 row 3b660ba0 are 8b4215c3 and fce8f953 with the BD-200 timeline wait change (27ea1698, 615121c0) reverted: in ASSISTED mode the monitored fence waited for GPU completion in place of submission, and Quake II RTX lost 11 % of its frame rate. The x86 system Vulkan row 8b4215c3 is the tester.35 wow64 line 17de7ab1 with the BD-200 timeline wait fix (27ea1698), the BD-203 external buffer report (a840b31a), the BD-287 upload pad (a5877980), the BD-179 stopped-adapter fence wait (a52627c7) and its WoW64 host test (8b4215c3). The x64 system row fce8f953 is the tester.35 system line 5dea8835 with the same BD-200, BD-203, BD-287 and BD-179 changes (615121c0, 6db68699, 0a4e8070, fce8f953). Only the x64 row has the BD-202 live BO budget (c52af544), the BD-206 GDI present worker (8ef83ef7 to 407d95b6) and the unified APU heap of BD-028 (f21279b9, c7474d7b, b064e507). The x86 line has no unified-heap commit. The tester.35 pair before that: The x86 system Vulkan row 17de7ab1 is the tester.34 wow64 line 9d8168c9 with the single-file disk cache on Windows (BD-216, 17de7ab1), and the x64 system row 5dea8835 is the tester.34 system line de66c413 with the same change. The tester.34 x86 line 9d8168c9 is the tester.33 wow64 line 20d7c8c9 with the BD-254 preamble and gather-slot fixes (cbe8dc03, f9191318, 771c666b), the BD-201 BO lifetime host test (d58067a4 to e7fb7053) and the fixes it shares with the x64 system line de66c413 (tester.33 line ad130cc2 with the same BD-201 test, 85486b52 to 874d30b2): the async compute threadgroup workaround on GFX1013 (x86 c0c1f240, x64 1f3f6938), the gfx1013 lowering of signed packed 4x8 dot products ported from dmorazasanchez/bc250-fsr4 v3 (x86 0f49b0ee to 8c452da1, x64 7ffc66ef to 67d3864e), driconf regular expressions on Windows, the process name at any path length, machine-profile driconf files, the per-application graphics settings, no GDS access without a GDS partition (BD-119), debugging variables read only in the lab flavour and the zstd 1.5.7 wrap. Only the x86 row reads MemoryOverflow and the WSI route switch in the 64-bit registry view (the x64 row reads that view natively). Only the x64 row has the compute-node border colour fix (3a5e0436) and the BD-212 fix that keeps the progress fence of a queue that goes with unretired work (fa4fadf7); the x64 row gets the instruction-prefetch padding (e92476c8) that the x86 line has had since before tester.33 (b3e45baf). The x86 settings reader uses the GDI-only WSI: MaxFrameLatency applies only to other GPUs on the DXGI path, and VSync 0 only skips the DWM wait. The x86 build does not port the x64 DXGI present or compute work.
